messages:
maria (Support): FYI @channel — NimbusPay (T-TENANT-42) opened a high-sev ticket: sustained 429s from their Dedicated pool in dp-west-2b starting ~10:15 UTC. Customer says latency spikes + 429s correlate with long chat sessions. They pasted a short log and a couple sample request IDs.

leo (Support): Can you drop the tenant id, pool name, model variant, and whether they did any recent deploys? Also any CPU/GPU pressure from the pool?

maria (Support): Tenant: T-TENANT-42, Pool: dp-west-2b-ded-1, Model: redwood/open-7b-q4_0 (pinned). No deploys today on their side. They said typical requests are long context (many > 30k tokens). Attached their minimal logs: 

```
[10:16:02] 429 response for req_id=abc123, reason="kv-cache-evict-throttle"
[10:16:02] kvcache.evictions=21234
[10:16:02] kvcache.kv_bytes_alloc=17.2GB
[10:16:02] heap_frag_percent=41
```

sanjay (eng-runtime): Thanks. From infra metrics for dp-west-2b-ded-1 we've got matching spikes. Evictions/sec and slab compaction events line up with the 429 window. Looks like KV-cache churn from very long contexts + a hot-prefix pattern -> eviction storms. We also see mem fragmentation creeping up.

kate (eng-sre): If it's a hot prefix problem, the eviction loop can cause temporary capacity loss and then autoscaler sees high load and throttles. Quick question: are requests pinning large KV caches per session (sticky sessions)?

maria (Support): Yes customer uses sticky sessions for long conversations — many open sessions with long histories. They also use many small function/tool calls interleaved.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Repro checklist I'm running now locally against a staging pool: create ~200 concurrent sessions, each with a 40k-token prefix and frequent context appends. Repro curl (example) for engineering: 

```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
     -H "x-tenant-id: T-TENANT-42" \
     -H "x-dedicated-pool: dp-west-2b-ded-1" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @long_prompt.json \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

long_prompt.json contains a repeated ~30k token prefix to simulate sessions.

kate (eng-sre): Short-term mitigation for customer: 1) advise them to reduce max_context or rotate older messages into embeddings (summary) 2) switch to a model variant with smaller KV footprint (if available) 3) we can enable tenant-level soft-throttling to smooth the burst (apply quota burst cap) — will need ops approval.

leo (Support): I've sent the recommended mitigation steps to the customer (suggest summary + lower max_context). They asked if we can do anything on our side to avoid future 429s while they refactor.

sanjay (eng-runtime): On our side we can: 
- temporarily relax aggressive slab compaction thresholds for dp-west-2b-ded-1 to avoid large synchronous evictions
- enable per-tenant LRU bias (favor pinned prefixes) for T-TENANT-42
- add a temporary routing rule to move new long-context sessions to a pool with more spare cache headroom
These are invasive; I need eng-sre signoff for a temporary config change.

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-8472, priority=P2, owner=sanjay (eng-runtime)

kate (eng-sre): I can do the config change after a short blackout window. Plan: schedule a 10-min config flip (non-disruptive) to relax compaction and enable LRU bias for the tenant, monitor evictions for 30m, roll back if we see negative impact. Also will add a transient rate limit at the ASG level to prevent autoscale thrash.

maria (Support): Customer approved a maintenance window in 45m. They also asked about a permanent solution to avoid this in future.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Permanent options to propose to product/customer: 
- recommend session summarization + embedding storage for very long chats (reduces KV footprint)
- offer a dedicated larger KV pool / increase reserved cache size for the tenant (commercial option)
- implement an auto-detect threshold that switches long-context requests to a streaming/partial-KV path to avoid full prefix retention

leo (Support): For the customer next steps I'm sending: (1) follow the short-term mitigations (2) accept our proposed maintenance window (3) consider summarization plan. I'll include the reproduction curl and the metrics snapshot.

kate (eng-sre): Action items: 
- kate: prep and schedule the 10-min config change (all changes will be logged)
- sanjay: prepare rollback and monitor dashboards, increase alert thresholds temporarily
- maria/leo: coordinate customer comms and capture sample requests for postmortem

maria (Support): Noted. Assigning owner: sanjay for engineering change, kate for ops execution. I'll update the ticket and post after the window. :thumbsup:

nimbuspay-ops: thanks — we'll also start a migration plan to shorten retained history and test the summarization approach. Appreciate the fast triage. :pray:

sanjay (eng-runtime): I'll post the post-deploy metrics here after the config flip. Expecting lower evictions and smoother autoscale behavior if hypothesis is correct.

maria (Support): Closing loop here once we verify. Leaving thread open for post-change results.
